newsitem.title: UK: BTR falls, continues to be out of favour.
newsitem.headline: BTR falls, continues to be out of favour.

text.p: Shares in BTR Plc fell to near their lowest level for more than five years as the diversified conglomerate continued to be out of favour with investors following last month's profit warning, dealers said.
BTR shares fell 2p to 195p by 1422 GMT in volume of almost 25 million shares, making it the most active stock in London's FTSE 100 index at that point.
But dealers pointed out 16.2 million shares of the volume was a "bed-and-breakfast," trade where an investor sells a stock but buys it straight back to realise a loss for tax purposes.
On Wednesday the shares touched 194p, their lowest level for more than five years.
Shares in BTR have slid almost continually since early May when the company warned the strength of sterling and weak conditions in key markets would dent sales and operating profits.
"Once a company issues a profit warning, it tends to stick," said one dealer. "It takes time to shake off the bad image."
The shares were undermined further by a huge placing of 80 million shares on May 8, the same day it issued its fifth profit warning in the past three years.
BTR said if the pound remained at current levels it would cut the company's first half sales in 1997 by about 300 million stg and operating profit by some 35 million pounds.
Sterling has since maintained its value against a basket of currencies with its trade weighted index currently at 99.6 compared with 99.7 at the beginning of last month.
